items.summary: Video provides a natural source of supervision: what happens next serves as a learning signal for visual world modeling. Yet masked video pretraining focuses on recovering missing content from surrounding context rather than predicting the future from the past. Autoregressive methods instead predict forward one token at a time, but have yet to match joint-embedding methods in representation quality. This gap motivates us to revisit the granularity and space of future prediction. In this work, we introduce VANE, a self-supervised visual pretraining framework built on next-frame prediction in embedding space. A causal encoder summarizes past observations for a state predictor that infers the representation of the entire next frame, making temporal evolution the primary learning signal. This prediction is carried out in a fixed embedding space provided by a frozen semantic tokenizer, emphasizing scene content and structure. To retain fine-grained spatial detail alongside semantic content, a lightweight auxiliary generative decoder reconstructs future-frame patches conditioned on the predicted representations. To unify visual modeling across images and videos, we construct a local-to-global crop sequence for still images, allowing the same encoder to predict newly revealed regions from earlier crops under the same objective. Experiments show that VANE improves with model and data scaling, achieving SOTA on most anticipation, recognition, and dense perception benchmarks among unified encoders. Especially on EPIC-KITCHENS-100 action anticipation, it surpasses V-JEPA 2.1 by 7.1 points in mean-class recall@5. These results demonstrate that next-frame prediction in embedding space is effective and scalable for visual world modeling.
items.title: Learning from Next-Frame Prediction: Towards Unified and Scalable Visual Representation Learning

items.summary: Supplementary methods, results, data tables and analysis code for the manuscript Inflammatory and NRF2-associated transcriptional responses in human intracerebral hemorrhage: paired myeloid evidence and gene-set sensitivity. The five resources contain supplementary methods, tables and figures, detailed data workbooks, reproducibility code and supporting audit documentation. Original code is licensed under MIT; original documentation and derived content are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Third-party materials retain their source terms; see LICENSES.md and source notices inside Online_Resource_3.zip. Manuscript abstract Public intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) datasets cover different tissue compartments and measure different subsets of genes, complicating comparisons across studies. We compared four specified gene sets (inflammation, complement, microglial activation and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2)-associated oxidative stress) in public paired human brain, single-cell and hematoma-effluent/blood datasets, using patients rather than cells as inferential units. In two studies of paired brain tissue, inflammation, complement and NRF2-associated scores were higher in perihematomal than contralateral samples in all four patient blocks and five matched pairs. Patient-level single-cell comparisons found higher inflammatory and complement scores in microglia/monocyte groups than in comparator lineages. In 14 patients with same-hour paired CD14+ and neutrophil data, a five-gene score named for microglial activation showed a positive CD14+–neutrophil local-response interaction in all 14 (adjusted P=0.000488), but four-program heterogeneity was not established (Friedman P=0.0796). Restricting this score to three shared genes reversed its CD14+ local response; a jointly scaled three-gene interaction was near zero. Independent acute blood data showed positive case-control differences, whereas longitudinal changes were not significant after adjustment. Inflammatory and NRF2-associated expression differences recurred across these datasets. The CD14+ local response of the microglial-related score depended on its measured genes. items.summary: Malaria early-warning systems that treat climate as a spatially uniform forcing mis-time vector-control deployment when the thermal niche of Anopheles vectors shifts across districts. The framework is formalised as a structural causal model over a district-month lattice, with a graph-identification condition and a lag-recovery theorem that bounds timing error by the spectral gap of the estimated adjacency matrix. A climate-analytics evaluation is conducted on NASA POWER monthly reanalysis air temperature at 2 m for Kampala, Uganda (0.35°N, 32.58°E), 2000–2023, comprising 312 monthly observations with a mean of 22.443 °C and a standard deviation of 1.043 °C; the estimated linear trend was −0.1564 °C per decade. The evaluation shows that a causal graph that admits lagged hydrological mediators recovers the intervention window with lower timing error than a temperature-only baseline, and that the error bound tightens as the spectral gap widens. The contribution is a formal link between causal-graph identifiability and the operational quantity that public-health managers actually care about: how many weeks early or late a spraying or net-distribution campaign is triggered.
tags: malaria early warning; causal graph learning; spatiotemporal modelling; climate analytics; intervent
items.title: Spatiotemporal causal graph learning for malaria early-warning under climate-driven vector-range shifts: a climate-analytics evaluation of intervention-timing error

items.summary: Despite significant advances in deep learning-based failure prognosis, existing predictive maintenance frameworks consistently terminate at the prediction step, leaving the critical operational challenge of prioritising maintenance resources across heterogeneous asset fleets unresolved. This paper addresses this gap by proposing an integrated framework that couples Long Short-Term Memory network-based Remaining Useful Life prediction with the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution for data-driven multi-criteria maintenance scheduling, validated on the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 turbofan degradation benchmark. The framework dynamically synthesises predicted health indicators with operational criteria encompassing machine criticality, maintenance cost, and production downtime impact to generate a ranked intervention schedule whose quality is evaluated through a rigorous, assumption-free protocol comprising precision-recall analysis, area under the precision-recall curve, Spearman rank correlation, and a scheduling efficiency ratio against a random baseline. A five-seed ablation study comparing Long Short-Term Memory, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, and Gated Recurrent Unit architectures, with Wilcoxon signed-rank validation, establishes statistically equivalent prediction accuracy, confirming the architecture-agnostic nature of the scheduling design.
items.title: Code and analysis: A Deep Learning and TOPSIS Framework for Predictive Maintenance Scheduling in Smart Manufacturing: An Industry 4.0 Approach

items.summary: World Models (WMs) can support Multimodal Agents (MAs) through simulated experience, while Agent trajectories can inform World Model refinement. Evaluating this interaction requires separate evidence about action selection and state evolution. We introduce Dual Exam, which tests Agents under fixed environment response mechanisms and World Models under fixed action interventions across physical, digital, social, and scientific domains. The Agent track compares 10 configurations on 1,088 items in 15 reporting categories. The World Model track contains 400 cases across eight scenarios; 15 configurations have full coverage and one covers six scenarios. GPT 6 Astra leads the case-weighted Agent Index at 31.3, and GPT-Image-2 leads the full-coverage WM Overall at 21.7. These scores use different tasks and metrics and are not directly comparable. A 150-case pilot of one coupled pairing records zero task successes and motivates component-level diagnosis. Results reveal uneven task performance and failures to preserve task-relevant state. Their value for predicting coupled success or sustained reciprocal learning remains to be established.
items.title: Dual Exam: Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Agents and World Models

items.summary: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn world models in latent space, enabling efficient planning but leaving their states opaque. We introduce Inside-JEPA, which places relational channels for ordered entity pairs inside the JEPA latent state and shows that an inverse-dynamics loss can ground these channels without relation labels when its head reads them, either alone or as part of the full state. On Something-Something V2, latent prediction alone performs no better than a random relation head, while inverse-dynamics supervision that recovers actions from channel changes improves relational AUROC by .065-.103 across ten settings with annotated boxes, by .081 on RH20T robot episodes with held-out tasks, and by .050-.061 across five relations using off-the-shelf detection and tracking. An inverse head on entity latents decodes actions more accurately but barely improves relational grounding; shuffled labels, two label-free objectives, and action labels on only 5% of the pairs also fail to ground the channels. Given an action, predicted relational changes approach the quality of observed future relations (AUROC .599 vs .621). For one-step relational goals, a supervised readout of the 16 channels ranks the correct action among the top five of 65 in 43% of cases, compared with 24% for prediction-only latents and 17% for a frequency prior.
items.title: Inside-JEPA: From Prediction to Relational Grounding in Latent World Models

items.summary: EnzyPair is a benchmark dataset for evaluating enzyme-function similarity at low sequence identity. items.title: EnzyPair: a dataset of same-function enzyme pairs with structure-matched controls at low sequence identity

items.summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Twenty-five entries are documented, nine of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, and a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten. Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, and carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters.
items.title: jerlov: inherent optical properties of the Jerlov optical water types, with provenance

items.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are increasingly proposed for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes, yet their behaviour under sparse radiosonde initialization remains poorly characterised for dam-safety analytics, where the upper tail of the rainfall distribution governs spillway design. We define the tail-index distortion functional, derive a bound on its bias under sparse initialization, and show that the distortion is governed by the interaction between the PINN's physics residual weighting and the effective sample size of the initial-condition ensemble. The framework is illustrated with a reanalysis-based temperature series for Lagos, Nigeria (2000–2023; 312 monthly observations; mean 26.414 °C; warming trend 0.1553 °C per decade), which serves as a benchmark for the data-provenance and uncertainty-reporting protocol that dam-safety analytics requires. Tail-index distortion should be treated as a first-class evaluation metric alongside predictive accuracy, and it identifies the conditions under which sparse radiosonde initialization produces non-conservative design quantiles. The contribution is a methodological and conceptual apparatus for auditing PINN downscaling in safety-critical climate analytics, not an empirical validation of any particular PINN architecture.
tags: physics-informed neural networks; rainfall extremes; tail-index distortion; dam safety; radiosonde i
items.title: Physics-informed neural networks for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes under sparse radiosonde initialization: a climate-analytics evaluation of tail-index distortion in dam-safety analytics

items.summary: Virtualization-based obfuscation and Mixed Boolean-Arithmetic (MBA) represent the modern standard for software intellectual property concealment and malware defense evasion, transforming native machine instructions into pseudo-random bytecodes executed by an embedded interpreter. Existing deobfuscation paradigms remain fundamentally brittle: dynamic execution tracing achieves incomplete path coverage while triggering anti-analysis defenses; classical Dynamic Symbolic Execution (DSE) suffers from catastrophic path explosion and prohibitive SMT solver latency over modular bit-vector arithmetic; and virtual stack mechanics leave hundreds of dead operations that overwhelm industry decompilers. In this paper, we present AETHER-64, a fully automated, static bytecode-driven devirtualization and algebraic simplification framework engineered specifically for 64-bit protected binaries. AETHER-64 introduces three foundational innovations: (1) Local-Context Handler Symbolic Slicing, which reconstructs complete Control-Flow Graphs (CFGs) through isolated basic block emulation without accumulating global path constraints; (2) a bit-parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction (APR) filter grounded in Boolean conjunction lattice signatures and fast Moebius inversion over Z/2^64, resolving invariant dispatch conditions in O(1) time; and (3) syntax-directed I/O-guided non-linear MBA synthesis coupled with LLVM Static Single Assignment (SSA) virtual stack elimination. We evaluate AETHER-64 on the Quarkslab Diffing Obfuscation Dataset (104 ground-truth functions across MiniLua, Zlib, and SQLite comprising 56,883 bytecode instructions), 1,000 synthetic Tigress virtual machines, commercial protections (VMProtect 3.4/3.5, Themida 3.1), and 7-layer non-linear MBA expressions. AETHER-64 achieves 100% CFG recovery, resolves 93.91% of branch queries via APR filtering with an empirical 2,072.8x speedup over raw SMT resolution, eliminates 91.8% of instruction bloat, and reconstructs clean, human-verifiable C pseudocode with mathematical bisimulation guarantees.
items.title: AETHER-64: High-Throughput Binary Devirtualization via Bit-Parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction and SSA Bytecode Promotion

items.summary: From Reversible Bit-Rings to Quantitative Matter Readouts The Qu Relational Compiler, Three-Dimensional Steric Closure, and Symmetry-Reduced Polymer Mechanics   Driven by Dean A. Kulik October, 2025   1. The Architectural Shift: From State Catalogs to Relational Compilation A foundational problem across discrete mathematics, quantum simulation, and macromolecular physics is distinguishing between a static state catalog and an executable transformation architecture. Conventional computational models treat physical configurations as external data structures submitted to an independent processor: conformations are enumerated in an address table, transitions are assigned by ad hoc hopping matrices or stochastic Monte Carlo rules, and empirical parameters are fitted post hoc to bulk observables. While effective for descriptive curve-fitting, that paradigm divorces the representation of a state from the lawful operations that generate and invert it. Whenever a coarse observation projects away an internal degree of freedom, a state-only model mistakes an observational quotient or a scheduling collision for an absolute physical barrier. The research program consolidated in this report—spanning the native binary partner rings, the One Inverter twisted clock, the Way Between three-dimensional conformational compiler, and the tetrahedral diamond-lattice and polyethylene matter readers through §167—establishes a rigorous alternative: compilation is the continuing resolution of local relational constraints, and physical observables are typed readouts of the resulting operator algebra. Rather than postulating an external machine or assigning arbitrary binary labels to particles, the architecture begins with the minimal condition for a distinction to persist without terminal fixed points ( ) and traces the exact algebraic and geometric structures forced at each scale. This progression unfolds across four interconnected operational tiers that preserve an explicit way home at every scale by pairing a quotient difference reader with a retained frame or phase coordinate. In the first tier, the native binary ring and twisted clock establish divided left and right representative hemispheres and forward/reverse faces governed by fixed-point-free involutions. In the second tier, the planar honeycomb route compiler lifts into a three-dimensional control torus where synchronous bond torsions execute a diagonal bypass around blocked planar corners. In the third tier, three-dimensional tetrahedral chains on the diamond lattice form an unbranched two-sheeted mirror quotient across a central reflection plane. In the fourth tier, the local tetrahedral operations and reflection symmetries collapse the 72-state polyethylene rotational-isomeric-state transfer matrix into four scalar coordinates, resolving the inverse parameter problem via a rank-two observable Jacobian. Across all four tiers, the compiler operates through two governing equations that separate the underlying accumulated transformation from the perspective of a particular observer: In the first equation, local reversible increments —whether bit shifts, modular carries, planar turns, or spatial   bond torsions—accumulate relative to a held reference frame . Changing   reorients the global description rigidly without altering any internal relation , while substituting a subword   with an alternative sequence   having the identical running product produces a strictly local transformation whose exterior remains undisturbed. In the second equation, the multiplicity structure   belongs to the object's own relation complex, while a chosen reader   exposes only the projection . An apparent zero in   or a rank deficiency in a planar Jacobian does not imply the absence of a physical continuation; it diagnoses a specific mismatch between the active transformation and the reader's coordinate chart. Every result included in this synth

items.summary: GradLint is a fast, standalone Rust-based command-line tool and Python package for diffusion MRI gradient-table quality control. It audits FSL and MRtrix gradient schemes, detects b-vector flip and axis-permutation errors using DWI image evidence, and writes corrected gradient tables with machine-readable provenance. GradLint is designed as a QC gate before diffusion MRI preprocessing, reconstruction, or tractography pipelines. It checks whether the supplied gradient table is geometrically consistent with the diffusion image, reports scheme-quality issues such as shell structure, direction counts, b0 handling, non-unit b-vectors, and angular sampling, and identifies silent convention errors that can otherwise propagate into tensor fitting and tractography results. The core detection method ranks signed axis permutations of the gradient table by a fibre-coherence criterion derived from a diffusion tensor fit. Candidate conventions are evaluated in the appropriate image or world frame for the input format: FSL bvec/bval tables are treated as image-relative, while MRtrix .b tables are treated as world-coordinate gradients. With audit --apply-repair, GradLint can write corrected FSL bvec/bval files and, optionally, an MRtrix .b table, together with JSON provenance describing the decision, transform, inputs, and outputs. WARN decisions additionally require --force-repair. Without --apply-repair, nonidentity corrections are withheld with an overall WARN and exit code 3. GradLint does not verify volume-to-gradient pairing. The software is implemented as a Rust core with thin command-line and Python interfaces. The Python package exposes the same functionality as the CLI and can render JSON reports to Markdown or HTML. Input gradient files are never modified in place unless an explicit overwrite option is used. This record archives the source code for GradLint v1.1.7, corresponding to the GitHub release published on 2026-10-23. The archived source includes the Rust core, CLI, Python bindings, report rendering layer, tests, CI/release metadata, and example materials included in the public source tree. items.summary: This protocol presents a systematic, deterministic translation framework for Beinecke MS 408 (The Voynich Manuscript). The framework interprets the manuscript as a 15th-century reverse-indexed chemical and pharmaceutical register produced within an Alpine/Central European workshop tradition. By operating on a phonetic-Latin reconstruction model, the cipher maps Extensible Alphabet Code (EVA) glyphs to a rigid, cross-sectional technical vocabulary. The validity of this protocol is verified through a 4-stage empirical pipeline featuring dual botanical cross-validation (Dragon's Blood resin vs. Opium Poppy latex) and external vernacular anchor verification via the marginalia on Folio 116v.
items.title: Voynich Manuscript Final Decoding Procedure

items.summary: Supplementary methods, results, data tables and analysis code for the manuscript Inflammatory and NRF2-associated transcriptional responses in human intracerebral hemorrhage: paired myeloid evidence and gene-set sensitivity. The five resources contain supplementary methods, tables and figures, detailed data workbooks, reproducibility code and supporting audit documentation. Original code is licensed under MIT; original documentation and derived content are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Third-party materials retain their source terms; see LICENSES.md and source notices inside Online_Resource_3.zip. Manuscript abstract Public intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) datasets cover different tissue compartments and measure different subsets of genes, complicating comparisons across studies. We compared four specified gene sets (inflammation, complement, microglial activation and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2)-associated oxidative stress) in public paired human brain, single-cell and hematoma-effluent/blood datasets, using patients rather than cells as inferential units. In two studies of paired brain tissue, inflammation, complement and NRF2-associated scores were higher in perihematomal than contralateral samples in all four patient blocks and five matched pairs. Patient-level single-cell comparisons found higher inflammatory and complement scores in microglia/monocyte groups than in comparator lineages. In 14 patients with same-hour paired CD14+ and neutrophil data, a five-gene score named for microglial activation showed a positive CD14+–neutrophil local-response interaction in all 14 (adjusted P=0.000488), but four-program heterogeneity was not established (Friedman P=0.0796). Restricting this score to three shared genes reversed its CD14+ local response; a jointly scaled three-gene interaction was near zero. Independent acute blood data showed positive case-control differences, whereas longitudinal changes were not significant after adjustment. Inflammatory and NRF2-associated expression differences recurred across these datasets. The CD14+ local response of the microglial-related score depended on its measured genes. Version 2026-10-24 changes This revision aligns the five supplementary resources with the current manuscript and adds the exact GSE163256 primary fractional-count-to-score reconstruction and fresh-score downstream verification. Earlier domain-score displays in Online Resource 2, worksheets 05 and 06, are replaced by the fixed-program paired-brain results already used in the manuscript. Superseded, undocumented competitive-null fields are removed from the current Puy13 summary display and export; the defined manufacturer-panel-matched analysis is retained. Scoring and provenance descriptions, archive entry points, fonts, table formatting and numerical display precision have also been corrected. The primary biological scores and current inferential statistics are unchanged. Earlier inputs and execution records are retained with their historical roles identified.
items.title: Reproducibility materials for Inflammatory and NRF2-associated transcriptional responses in human intracerebral hemorrhage: paired myeloid evidence and gene-set sensitivity

Its central coupling is mission evidence x metrological traceability x release contract. A successful demonstration is not treated as an engineering release: every decisive quantity must retain raw ancestry, calibration, uncertainty, protocol version, software identity, failure context, and independent adjudication. The central artifact is the Mission Qualification Capsule. It binds the reference mission, operating domain, hardware and lot genealogy, immutable raw event streams, digital calibration objects, covariance, provenance graph, software and configuration manifests, failure ontology, missingness, terminal functional evidence, threshold history, change control, negative results, and release ruling. A second laboratory should be able to reproduce the metric, failure classification, and final action without private communication from the original authors.

items.summary: Video provides a natural source of supervision: what happens next serves as a learning signal for visual world modeling. Yet masked video pretraining focuses on recovering missing content from surrounding context rather than predicting the future from the past. Autoregressive methods instead predict forward one token at a time, but have yet to match joint-embedding methods in representation quality. This gap motivates us to revisit the granularity and space of future prediction. In this work, we introduce VANE, a self-supervised visual pretraining framework built on next-frame prediction in embedding space. A causal encoder summarizes past observations for a state predictor that infers the representation of the entire next frame, making temporal evolution the primary learning signal. This prediction is carried out in a fixed embedding space provided by a frozen semantic tokenizer, emphasizing scene content and structure. To retain fine-grained spatial detail alongside semantic content, a lightweight auxiliary generative decoder reconstructs future-frame patches conditioned on the predicted representations. To unify visual modeling across images and videos, we construct a local-to-global crop sequence for still images, allowing the same encoder to predict newly revealed regions from earlier crops under the same objective. Experiments show that VANE improves with model and data scaling, achieving SOTA on most anticipation, recognition, and dense perception benchmarks among unified encoders. Especially on EPIC-KITCHENS-100 action anticipation, it surpasses V-JEPA 2.1 by 7.1 points in mean-class recall@5. These results demonstrate that next-frame prediction in embedding space is effective and scalable for visual world modeling.
items.title: Learning from Next-Frame Prediction: Towards Unified and Scalable Visual Representation Learning

The author independently reviewed the cited sources, equations, numerical procedures, computational results, scientific interpretations and final claims, and accepts full responsibility for the content. AI-assisted output was not treated as evidence, and computational verification was evaluated separately from physical evidence.

items.summary: Despite significant advances in deep learning-based failure prognosis, existing predictive maintenance frameworks consistently terminate at the prediction step, leaving the critical operational challenge of prioritising maintenance resources across heterogeneous asset fleets unresolved. This paper addresses this gap by proposing an integrated framework that couples Long Short-Term Memory network-based Remaining Useful Life prediction with the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution for data-driven multi-criteria maintenance scheduling, validated on the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 turbofan degradation benchmark. The framework dynamically synthesises predicted health indicators with operational criteria encompassing machine criticality, maintenance cost, and production downtime impact to generate a ranked intervention schedule whose quality is evaluated through a rigorous, assumption-free protocol comprising precision-recall analysis, area under the precision-recall curve, Spearman rank correlation, and a scheduling efficiency ratio against a random baseline. A five-seed ablation study comparing Long Short-Term Memory, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, and Gated Recurrent Unit architectures, with Wilcoxon signed-rank validation, establishes statistically equivalent prediction accuracy, confirming the architecture-agnostic nature of the scheduling design.
items.title: Code and analysis: A Deep Learning and TOPSIS Framework for Predictive Maintenance Scheduling in Smart Manufacturing: An Industry 4.0 Approach

items.summary: World Models (WMs) can support Multimodal Agents (MAs) through simulated experience, while Agent trajectories can inform World Model refinement. Evaluating this interaction requires separate evidence about action selection and state evolution. We introduce Dual Exam, which tests Agents under fixed environment response mechanisms and World Models under fixed action interventions across physical, digital, social, and scientific domains. The Agent track compares 10 configurations on 1,088 items in 15 reporting categories. The World Model track contains 400 cases across eight scenarios; 15 configurations have full coverage and one covers six scenarios. GPT 6 Astra leads the case-weighted Agent Index at 31.3, and GPT-Image-2 leads the full-coverage WM Overall at 21.7. These scores use different tasks and metrics and are not directly comparable. A 150-case pilot of one coupled pairing records zero task successes and motivates component-level diagnosis. Results reveal uneven task performance and failures to preserve task-relevant state. Their value for predicting coupled success or sustained reciprocal learning remains to be established.
items.title: Dual Exam: Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Agents and World Models

items.summary: RFT-FaultBench provides training-process telemetry for anomaly detection and failure-type diagnosis in reinforcement fine-tuning. This revised dataset contains 2,630 runs (339 normal and 2,291 injected), 72,100 train-step records, and 2,617,600 training trajectories across OpenRLHF, AgentEvolver, and TRL and five task categories: arithmetic reasoning, GSM8K-style mathematical reasoning, code generation, verifiable instruction following, and tool calling. It includes 55 compound-failure runs for detection; diagnosis uses 2,236 single-failure runs. Task versions and native failure-label coverage differ across frameworks. The package includes run-level artifacts, canonical labels and seeds, five seed-grouped evaluation folds, 25 one-shot support draws, provenance and exclusion ledgers, per-file checksums, and Python example loaders and validation tools. Membership follows the frozen 2026-10-12 evaluation snapshot. It updates the earlier 779-run release; no new training was performed during packaging. GitHub companion: AIOps4LLM/RFT-FaultBench . Related manuscript: Towards Robust LLM Post-Training: Automatic Failure Diagnosis for Reinforcement Fine-Tuning. Extract RFT-FaultBench-full.tar.gz and consult its README and docs for schemas, verification evidence, and evaluation scope. The dataset continues the CC BY 4.0 license of the preceding Zenodo version.
items.title: RFT-FaultBench-full

items.summary: This paper develops the Phase Compatibility branch of Harmonic Physics: a framework for examining how physical participants enter constrained phase relations, produce collective outcomes, and form persistent higher-level organisations capable of further recursive participation. Building on established synchronization theory, phase locking, coupled-oscillator dynamics and phasor mathematics, the framework examines reinforcement, opposition, cancellation, reshaping and whole formation. It distinguishes mathematical admissibility, actual source occupancy, participant admission, active interaction, closure, continuing identity and observation. A compatibility basin is characterised through maintained relational organisation and persistence under declared conditions. Version 3.1 aligns the shared definitions with the current Foundations and Observer Theory papers, corrects the amplitude-weighted moment family, and clarifies the distinction between passive changes of representation and physical projection or coupling. It incorporates the completed mathematical nesting construction, which preserves a supplied quantum state’s amplitude and relative-phase information, together with Born probabilities under corresponding joint measurements. Phase Theory Equations is identified as the consolidated reference for the current mathematical expressions. The observation account separates source organisation, information encoded into light, receiver coupling, registration, retention and calibrated reconstruction. Within the proposed optical terminology, light performs the observer role through source–receiver coupling, while the receiver registers and retains a physical response. Minimal relational consciousness and awareness retain separate definitions. The paper integrates controlled models, molecular spectral studies, a superconducting-qubit analogue, simulated liquid-water reorganisation, quantum-state encoding and specified receiver models, preserving the scope and limitations of each result. It sets out the state spaces, conservation requirements, comparison models and prospective failure conditions required for physical applications. Universal participant-admission and whole-formation laws remain open research questions; this revision introduces no new experimental validation.
items.title: Phase Compatibility: Harmonic Combination, Selective Participation, Whole Formation, and Recursive Organisation

items.summary: We study intransitive probabilistic preferences through dice whose face labels may be repeated. We distinguish restricted models, in which the set of permitted labels depends on the number of sides, from the unrestricted model, which allows arbitrary integer labels. We review existence results, including the exceptional impossibility of a Chinese chain of five four-sided dice, and give an explicit construction establishing the known existence of simple cycles of three-sided dice of every length m ≥3, with no ties and a net win margin of one. We examine mixed-integer programming, simulated annealing, and lexicographic optimization of the margins. We then extend pairwise comparison to probability measures by means of bounded, measurable, antisymmetric kernels. For complete comparison data with uniform weights, we derive the Hodge decomposition of the margin matrix into an additive score component and an orthogonal, divergence-free residual. We distinguish the failure of an exact additive representation from the existence of strict preference cycles. The minimax theorem ensures that every finite family admits a mixed strategy with nonnegative expected margin against every mixture of that family. For the historical cycle with margins 4, 4, 10, we compute both the decomposition and the equilibrium mixture (2/9, 5/9, 2/9). Applications to portfolios, artistic evaluation, visual perception, and sports clarify the distinctions among independent comparisons, shared scenarios, and expected utility.
items.title: Chinese and Mayan Dice: Circular Chains, Explicit Constructions, and Decision Theory

items.summary: IrrMapper is a Random Forest classification of Landsat imagery that maps irrigated agriculture each year at 30 m across Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Montana, New Mexico, Nevada, Oregon, Utah, Washington and Wyoming. This deposit is the GeoTIFF release of version 1.2, the product served in the Google Earth Engine public data catalog as UMT/Climate/IrrMapper_RF/v1_2. One zip per state holds one cloud-optimized GeoTIFF per year (450 files; California begins in 1986), the state boundary polygon used for clipping, and grids.json describing every state's raster grid. Values: 1 irrigated, 0 not irrigated, 255 nodata. All files are in EPSG:5070 (NAD83 / Conus Albers) at 30 m on one shared pixel lattice, so all years of a state stack without resampling and neighboring states align pixel for pixel. SHA256 checksums are provided for every GeoTIFF and archive. See README.md for the format, grid definition, provenance and known limitations.
items.title: IrrMapper v1.2: annual 30 m irrigated-agriculture maps of 11 western US states, 1985-2025

items.summary: ICMarkingSynthetic is a synthetic image dataset of defective integrated circuit markings generated by physics-informed guidelines. The guidelines distinguish surface abrasion and deposition from changes to the marking itself, covering scratch, contamination, missing text, smeared text, and combined defects. Images are accompanied by labels and generation provenance. These models are cause-derived image-formation approximations, not first-principles material or optical simulations. This record contains the dataset archive and its companion generator archive. Reproduction instructions and annotation limitations are documented in the archive READMEs. The record metadata are public; access to both archives is restricted. Reviewers and researchers may request access by contacting mdsamiul.hoque@utdallas.edu and describing their intended use. Access requests are reviewed individually. License scopes: image assets are licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 with per-source attribution; annotations and provenance are licensed under CC BY 4.0; the generator code is licensed under MIT. These licenses apply to their respective components and are not alternative licenses for every file.
items.title: ICMarkingSynthetic: A synthetic image dataset of defective integrated circuit markings generated by physics-informed guidelines

items.summary: Overview This repository contains the replication data, source code, execution logs, and complete analytical outputs for the study: “Detectability of controlled leaks in an Andean water transmission main: a field evaluation of changepoint methods on flow and pressure signals.” The study evaluates the detectability of short-duration controlled leaks using five changepoint and anomaly-detection approaches applied to 30-second flow and pressure measurements collected during two field campaigns in an operational water transmission main in Loja, Ecuador. The evaluated methods are: Pruned Exact Linear Time using the Bayesian Information Criterion (PELT-BIC), Pruned Exact Linear Time using the Akaike Information Criterion (PELT-AIC), Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection (BOCD), Cumulative Sum control charts (CUSUM), Moving-average ±3σ control-chart baseline. The repository contains the complete workflow used to: verify field records and ground-truth leak timings; perform campaign-specific spectral analyses using multitaper estimation; evaluate changepoint-detection performance; quantify event-level leak detectability; compare observed performance against chance-level expectations; assess BOCD sensitivity to hazard-rate and threshold settings; generate precision-recall curves and average-precision statistics; perform cross-campaign validation analyses; estimate theoretical detection-delay bounds for flow-based detection. This version supersedes earlier releases by correcting changepoint-index alignment, revising false-alarm-rate calculations using exposure time outside detection windows, replacing pooled spectral analyses with campaign-specific multitaper analyses, and incorporating event-level detectability, chance-level benchmarking, precision-recall evaluation, cross-campaign validation, and theoretical detection-delay analyses. Dataset Description The repository is organized into raw data files and compressed archives containing the complete computational environment and analytical outputs. 1. Primary Data (Raw) Q_P_80_Leak1.xlsx 30-second flow (Q) and pressure (P) measurements collected during the first controlled-leak field campaign. Q_P_46_Leak2.xlsx 30-second flow (Q) and pressure (P) measurements collected during the second controlled-leak field campaign. 2. Source Code and Execution Logs This archive contains: CHANGEPOINT_Rcode.R Complete R workflow for: data verification and screening; descriptive statistical analysis; event-level leak detectability assessment; multitaper spectral analysis; PELT-BIC and PELT-AIC changepoint detection; Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection (BOCD); CUSUM detection; moving-average ±3σ detection; chance-level benchmarking; hazard-rate × threshold sensitivity analysis; cross-campaign BOCD validation; precision-recall and average-precision analysis; theoretical detection-delay modelling. CHANGEPOINT_Console.txt Complete console log documenting: descriptive statistics; event-level detectability results; spectral-analysis outputs; changepoint locations; detector performance metrics; chance-level comparisons; precision-recall analyses; BOCD validation results; theoretical delay-bound calculations. 3. Model Outputs (analisis_output.zip) changepoint/ ground_truth_trials.csv detector_performance_by_trial.csv detector_performance_extended.csv detector_performance_pooled.csv hazard_threshold_sweep.csv bocd_cross_campaign.csv average_precision.csv pr_operating_points.csv mcnemar_signal.csv mcnemar_methods.csv spectral_summary.csv cusum_delay_bound.csv cusum_delay_curve.csv cusum_delay_mc_check.csv BOCD_Leak1_flow.csv BOCD_Leak1_pressure.csv BOCD_Leak2_flow.csv BOCD_Leak2_pressure.csv changepoint_objects.rds figures/ High-resolution TIFF figures (600 dpi): Fig7.tif: campaign-specific multitaper spectral analyses; Fig8.tif: flow and pressure time series with leak intervals and detected changepoints; Fig9.tif: BOCD posterior probabilities; Fig10.tif: detection lat

items.summary: Malaria early-warning systems that treat climate as a spatially uniform forcing mis-time vector-control deployment when the thermal niche of Anopheles vectors shifts across districts. The framework is formalised as a structural causal model over a district-month lattice, with a graph-identification condition and a lag-recovery theorem that bounds timing error by the spectral gap of the estimated adjacency matrix. A climate-analytics evaluation is conducted on NASA POWER monthly reanalysis air temperature at 2 m for Kampala, Uganda (0.35°N, 32.58°E), 2000–2023, comprising 312 monthly observations with a mean of 22.443 °C and a standard deviation of 1.043 °C; the estimated linear trend was −0.1564 °C per decade. The evaluation shows that a causal graph that admits lagged hydrological mediators recovers the intervention window with lower timing error than a temperature-only baseline, and that the error bound tightens as the spectral gap widens. The contribution is a formal link between causal-graph identifiability and the operational quantity that public-health managers actually care about: how many weeks early or late a spraying or net-distribution campaign is triggered.
tags: malaria early warning; causal graph learning; spatiotemporal modelling; climate analytics; intervent
items.title: Spatiotemporal causal graph learning for malaria early-warning under climate-driven vector-range shifts: a climate-analytics evaluation of intervention-timing error

items.summary: pt selection with a position-by-position wild-type amino-acid check; 4. a gene-level inflation test and a silent-mutation (synonymous) control that    distinguishes elevated local background mutation rate from positive selection. The archive contains 16 scripts in two groups. Group 1 (6 scripts) reproduces the filtering cascade, the neutral gene-set control, the TCGA MC3 replication and the reference-panel benchmark. Group 2 (10 scripts, numbered 20-29) implements the silent-mutation control reported in Table 8: donor-level observed/expected ratios, exact Poisson upper-tail P values, the non-silent-to-silent fold with a delta-method 95% confidence interval, and the coding-length-matched percentile. All machine-specific paths have been replaced by environment-overridable defaults (ARG_ROOT, ARG_ANALYSIS, ARG_SILENT); see 00_README.md. Inputs are entirely public (ICGC open-tier simple_somatic_mutation files; 1000 Genomes Phase 3; gnomAD v2.1.1; the TCGA MC3 public MAF). No credentials and no controlled-access data are required.
items.title: ARG-QC: quality-control pipeline for pharmacogene somatic-mutation analyses of open-access cancer genomics data

items.summary: PyUnitWizard 0.29.0 This additive release expands verified quantity exchange while retaining the existing computing APIs, session policy and qrec/0.3 / bundle bytes. Tagged QuantityRecord arrays share unit/kind descriptors; homogeneous immutable append checks conversion, dtype and trailing shape (#102/#105). Zarr snapshots support verified first-axis partial reads; typed Arrow tables and complete local Parquet bindings retain explicit unit/kind handshakes (#104/#103). Case-sensitive UCUM tools validate explicit output codes and import biomedical values through actual ucumvert 0.3.2 (#125). Only independently qualified physical atoms are admitted; unchecked provider aliases are refused. Native ASDF/Astropy quantities carry an additional sealed snapshot binding; readers check named unit meaning, SI scale, dtype/shape, value seals and their own expectations (#126). Explicit QUDT/UO annotations bind a record and selected identifiers to an offline attributed catalogue for hertz, becquerel and radians/second (#127). Quantity kinds are chosen by consumers, never inferred from SI dimensions. Earlier source fixes preserve OpenMM angstrom meaning in unyt, reuse unyt registries, preserve atomic-mass names/prefixes and record actual benchmark interpreter provenance (#120–#124). All record extensions, optional dialects/storage bindings, measurement statements and attribution surfaces remain provisional . New format identifiers are explicit; old readers must not interpret them as old formats. QUDT/UO correspondences are reviewed local alignments, not upstream exactMatch claims. Limits remain explicit: immutable append copies values; Zarr selection verifies selected chunk contents; Arrow nulls are refused and Parquet reads whole files. ASDF is homogeneous/multiplicative only; affine temperatures need explicit conversion to Kelvin. Unknown vocabularies, arbitrary/nonlinear/annotated UCUM units, CF calendar coordinates, full clinical/astronomy schemas and consumer migrations are outside this checkpoint. Seals establish integrity, not producer authentication or scientific truth of an asserted kind. Baseline support remains Linux/macOS arm64, Python 3.11–3.14. Optional profiles retain their own provider/interpreter constraints, including OpenFF 0.4.0 on Python 3.12–3.14 with Pint <0.26 and UCUM's Pint >=0.25 requirement. Exact source, immutable Conda artifact, installed matrix and publication receipts are tracked in release #128 . Publication of this version does not admit the provisional contracts as stable or establish adoption in consuming repositories. Publication identity: canonical annotated tag 0.29.0 , source cfe067bcc4545c60aaca4c6950f6d84075ee6c36 . All 29 required native source jobs passed, with actual CI coverage/test-result uploads and eight optional source-wheel probes passing 247 cases each without skips. Original Conda producer: 40014661788 , attempt 1. Exact file: pyunitwizard-0.29.0-py_0.tar.bz2 (94,325 bytes), SHA-256 9169cd302dbda415ebc441ef6f5077dcde834d435626fcf80c179a9013657f34 . All 30 installed cells plus the original-producer verifier passed 40018157605 . The distinct qualifier 821231dbf188656b6872b5f6866b20e9114c87fb is explicitly bound to the original source/file; the artifact was not rebuilt. Required storage/dialect and prepared-attribution modules executed without skips in their respective eight-cell profiles. Intentional strict-JSON/NaN and unavailable prepared-API skips elsewhere remain classified in retained JUnit evidence. At GitHub Release creation, the exact file is staged and public-main promotion is pending. Publication status, public installation/docs verification and client-guide handoff are updated in MolSysSuite #132 and release #128 .

items.summary: Motivation: Variant calling for next-generation sequencing (NGS) data relies on a diverse ecosystem of tools and workflows. Large-scale collaborative studies increasingly adopt federated analysis, where each institution processes sensitive data locally using standardized pipelines. Deploying identical pipelines across multiple centers remains challenging because heterogeneous software environments and computing policies can cause workflow divergence and inconsistent results. Results: We developed CBIcall, a workflow backend-flexible, configuration-driven framework that runs standardized variant-calling pipelines from raw FASTQ files to analysis-ready VCFs. Users define each analysis in a single YAML parameters file, which CBIcall resolves against a controlled workflow registry and resource catalog. The execution driver validates parameters and checks compatibility among pipelines, analysis modes, workflow backends, genome builds, tool versions, and resource bundles. CBIcall supports reproducibility auditing by comparing executions using recorded provenance and output fingerprints. CBIcall dispatches validated workflows natively through Bash, Cromwell, Nextflow and Snakemake backends and provides production-ready pipelines for germline WES, WGS (single-sample or cohort joint genotyping following GATK Best Practices), and mitochondrial DNA analysis. We evaluated analytical performance using public benchmark datasets and validated reproducibility across four computing environments. We further deployed CBIcall in the EU HEREDITARY project, where it processed 1102 samples with both WES and mtDNA pipelines on an institutional HPC system, supporting its suitability for reproducible cohort-scale genomic analyses. Availability and implementation: CBIcall is open source (GPLv3) and distributed with ready-to-run pipelines; full dependency and installation documentation is available at https://github.com/CNAG-Biomedical-Informatics/cbicall.
items.title: CBIcall: a configuration-driven framework for variant calling in large sequencing cohorts

items.summary: EnzyPair is a benchmark dataset for evaluating enzyme-function similarity at low sequence identity. It contains 1,664 same-EC4 protein pairs and 4,992 structure-matched different-EC4 controls involving 2,465 proteins. The release includes protein sequences, EC annotations, TM-align measurements, residue alignments, exclusion records, source provenance and software versions.
items.title: EnzyPair: a dataset of same-function enzyme pairs with structure-matched controls at low sequence identity

items.summary: Release notes - v2.3 This release refreshes the analysis layer, the result archives and the auditing tooling. It contains code, result archives and provenance metadata only. Included Analysis scripts ( tools/ ) environment-variance decomposition with a seed-level bootstrap; per-layer coupling analysis for a second vision-language backbone; third-family robustness controls (small Idefics3-family model) with multi-seed runs; exact permutation tests for extreme-rank comparisons; allocation-baseline reproductions, including a name-adapter port of an official allocator; a content-audit script that cross-checks reported values against the JSON archives; local environment scripts for torch 2.4/CUDA 12.1 and torch 2.6/CUDA 12.4. Result archives ( outputs/analysis/ , paper3/scripts/outputs/experiments/ ) environment matrix archives for four software stacks; variance-decomposition, permutation-test and per-layer coupling archives; third-family multi-seed archives; updated final-verification and provenance-gate reports. Tooling and metadata provenance metadata extended for the newly added result entries; release-notes and packaging housekeeping; audit script that verifies archived values against their source JSON. Verification all repository gates pass: frozen-archive hashes, provenance gate, claim ledger, per-project audits and the final verification report. Excluded (by repository policy) Model weights and datasets.
